description.content:
Bright Pattern's List Management API streamlines the creation and deletion of lists and formats and provides a convenient way to manage list records.

Note: Performing operations on lists requires the user to have the "Manage Lists" privilege, configured in the Contact Center Administrator application. Additional privileges required are explicitly specified in the corresponding method description.

All of the methods described below use the path variable, list_id, to specify the list an operation is to be performed on. The unique identifier of a list can be found by opening that list in the Contact Center Administrator application, Lists section. The id will be displayed in the '#LISTS:LISTS_PROPERTIES:' fragment of the URL.

Alternatively, list_id, can be found in the response body of the Get Lists method (see here).

Methods retained from the previous version of the List management API, tagged as "DEPRECIATED", require an additional path variable, campaign_id, to reference the campaign associated with the selected list. The unique identifier of a campaign can be found by opening that campaign in the Contact Center Administrator application, Services & Campaigns section. The id will be displayed in the '#SERVICES_CAMPAIGNS:SERVICES_PROPERTIES:' fragment of the URL.

Alternatively, campaign_id, can be found in the response body of the Get Campaigns method (see here).

Note: When importing records or updating records it is important to remember that:

All leading and trailing whitespaces should be deleted.

For all PHONE numbers:

If a number begins with “+”, the leading "+" sign will be removed.

If a number contains non-numeric characters, they will be removed.

At least one PHONE number is required.

For the United States and Canada PHONE numbers:

If a number begins with “011”, it will be kept as is.

If a number begins with “1” and has eleven digits, it will be kept as is.

If a number does not begin with “1” and has ten digits, “1” will be prepended.

If a number begins with “1” and has ten digits, the record will not be imported, returning a format error.

In any other case, the record will not be imported, returning a format error.

Remove prefix and Default country code fields will be ignored.

For Other countries PHONE numbers:

If a number begins with prefix matching Remove prefix, the prefix will be deleted.

If a number does not begin with prefix matching Remove prefix, it will be kept as is.

If a number does not begin with prefix matching Default country code, Default country code will be added.

For all INTEGER fields:

If the value is presented as a string, it should be converted to an integer.

Values presented as integers should be supported.

For all fields that expect strings (ACCOUNT, AGENT_LOGIN_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, etc.) integer values should be converted to strings.

Capitalization matters: values with different capitalizations are treated as distinct.

This method returns a list of records from a calling list associated with a campaign.

Records are referenced by indexes, assigned to each record in the list in sequential order of insertion (beginning from 0). All records with an index greater than or equal to the requested record index, fromIndex, are returned in the response.

Note: The returned recordset contains JSON objects sorted by the index field. List Record JSON Object has two sub-objects, entry and status, defined as follows:

entry object: contains a copy of the list entry

field names are retained as defined at list creation

custom fields are returned with the prefix 'custom_' added to the name defined in the Administrator Application

Note: The value returned in the id field can be used to reference this record in further API requests.

statusobject: contains the campaign results for this specific record

omitted if the list is not assigned to the campaign or the campaign doesn't exist

field names are predefined

completed field is always present, while the other fields may be absent if the record was never called or never reached an agent.

description.content:
This method returns a copy of an existing record in a calling list of an associated campaign. The list is specified in the path variable, list_id, by its unique identifier returned in the response body of the Get Campaign method (see here). The campaign is specified in the path variable, campaign_id, by its unique identifier returned in the response body of the Get Campaigns method (see here).

The record search is performed by its unique identifier, id, returned in the response body of the Get All Records method (see here). If the list has been added to the specified campaign more than once, the method returns an array of records. An error is returned if a record with the specified id does not exist in the selected list.

Note: The response body contains the List Record JSON Object, defined by two sub-objects as follows:

entry object: contains a copy of the list entry
field names are retained as defined at list creation
custom fields are returned with the prefix 'custom_' added to the name defined in the Administrator Application

time and date field values are returned in UTC format

statusobject: contains the campaign results for this specific record
omitted if the list is not assigned to the campaign or the campaign doesn't exist

field names are predefined

completed field is always present, while the other fields may be absent if the record was never called or never reached an agent.

Note: If a PHONE type field is defined as a key, the record value is checked for a full match with the value stored in the database or the original source (if the data was modified upon loading into the database).

Response Codes

Code
Description

200
Success

400
Bad request (format not understood; 1 or more required fields are missing or have an unsupported value)

401
Authentication failed (invalid token format; token is expired)

403
Authentication succeeded but the user does not have sufficient privileges

404
Specified List was not found;  
Specified Record was not found;  
Invalid URL

This method deletes a list, archiving all records with associated campaign results associated with that list. If the last list using a specific format was deleted, that format is removed as well.

Note: Bright Pattern Contact Center solution supports several voice campaign modes (see here). Depending on the mode of the associated campaign, the active call behavior will differentiate as follows:

Progressive, Predictive, or Automatic (IVR) campaigns
Upon instance deletion, all active, i.e. in a dialing state, within a script, or connected to an agent, calls are dropped

Preview campaigns
Upon instance deletion, only the calls not yet picked up by an agent are dropped. In-progress and connected calls are not affected

The results of completed calls are archived and available for downloading in the Contact Center Administrator application (see here). Interaction results for dropped calls are not saved.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

This method creates a new empty list and a new format corresponding to that list.

When creating the new list format, the fields must be defined with the following properties in mind:

Field Property
Description

name (string)
Required property that defines field names. The names must be unique.  
Default value: -

type (string)
Required property that indicates the type of data the field contains.  
Note: See the table below for available data types.  
Default value: -

required (boolean)
Optional property that indicates that the data in this field is required.  
Default value: false

searchable (boolean)
Optional property that indicates that this field will be used for record lookups.  
Default value: false

skip (boolean)
Optional property that indicates that the data in this field is non-essential. Such data will not be included in Campaign Results/Archives, returned in API requests, or imported into the database. However, including such fields in the request body should not result in an error since the fields are simply ignored.  
Note: Skipped fields cannot be set as required, searchable, or key.  
Default value: false

key (boolean)
Optional property that indicates that this field will be used to identify list records uniquely. The key will be used to detect duplicated and reference Campgin Results data.  
Default value: false

Note: The following properties are not used when the method is called: CUSTOM_DELIMITER(default 'COMMA' value is set), DEFAULT_ENCODING(default 'UTF-8' value is set), DELIMITER_TYPE, FORMAT_TYPE(default 'DELIMITED' value is set),NAMES_IN_FIRST_LINE, SOURCE_TYPE.

Field types

Field Type
Description

ACCOUNT
Account type fields can be used to store customer's unique identifiers. The values from such fields are stored in the Call History and can be used for interaction record search.  
Note: List formats can only have one field of this type.

AGENT_LOGIN_ID
Fields of this type are used to assign records to specific agents in preview and progressive campaign modes.  
Note: This field will be ignored if used in predictive or automatic campaigns.

CALLING_NUMBER
Fields of this type contain the numbers to be displayed as caller IDs when dialing the corresponding records from campaigns.  
NOTE: Fields of this type are required to enable the From list field of type "Caller ID" caller id assignment method.

COMPANY
Company type fields can be used to store the information about a business/company the record belongs to, e.g. company name.

DATETIME
Fields of this type can be used to specify the date and time a callback request was made. Typically, such information is provided in opt-in callback lists. Fields of this type have additional properties, timeZone and format.  
  
Supported formats:  
MM/dd/yyyy ::mm(Default);  
dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm;  
yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm;  
yyyy-MM-dd;  
dd-MM-yyyy;  
MM-dd-yyyy;  
MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss

DATETIME_CALL_AT
Fields of this type can be used to specify the date and time the record should be called. Fields of this type have additional properties, timeZone and format(see above for details about supported formats).

FIRST_NAME
Fields of this type store the first name of the contact.

INTEGER
Integer type fields store semantically numeric data, e.g. age or account balance. Such fields can be used to set campaign quotas.

LAST_NAME
Fields of this type store the last name of the contact.

OTHER
Other is used to specify that the field has a type different than the predefined types outlined here.

PHONE
Phone type fields store the phone numbers to be dialed during campaigns.  
Note: Fields of this type have additional properties defined in the table below.  
Note: List formats must have at least one Phone field defined.

ZIP_CODE
Fields of this type store the postal code of the contact.  
Note: Fields of this type are required to enable the Use safe calling hours setting.

PRIORITY
Priority type fields indicate that the record must be attempted before the other records in the list. Fileds of this type  
have additional properties:order,i.e. First-in-First-out or Last-in-FIrst-Out, andexpiresAfter,used to set the expiration date of the priority setting.

STATE
Fields of this type store the state the contact lives in.  
Note: Fields of this or the ZIP_CODE type are required to enable the Comply with State calling hours setting.

This method updates fields in an existing record of a calling list. Additionally, this method can reset an optional parameter to its default value by passing " " or null to that parameter.

Note: Manipulating the content of calling lists requires the user to have an additional "Update content of calling list" privilege.

The search for the record is performed based on the defined key fields. The request can contain either a full or partial set of fields of the List Record JSON Object, but the key fields are mandatory and must be retained as configured during list creation.

Before the record is queried, its existence in the specified list is checked by its unique key values. If the record does exist in the specified list, the record is updated successfully.

Note: If a PHONE type field is defined as a key, the record value is checked for a full match with the value stored in the database or the original source (if the data was modified upon loading into the database).

To avoid disruptions in the campaign work caused by the list reprocessing time, the Dialer ignores the changes made to the record until it makes a call attempt to that record. Thus, if a list containing the updated record has Filters or Sorting configured, the changes made to that record will not affect that filtering or sorting order.

Note: Always remember to reapply the desired Filters or Sorting settings if you wish for it to reflect the changes made to the updated record.

This method removes a record from a list and all associated campaign results. The search for the record is performed based on the defined key fields. An error is returned if a record does not exist.

Note: Manipulating the content of calling lists requires the user to have an additional "Update content of calling list" privilege.

Bright Pattern Contact Center solution supports several voice campaign modes (see here). If the last record is being deleted, depending on the mode of the associated campaign, the active call behavior will differentiate as follows:

Progressive, Predictive, or Automatic (IVR) campaigns
Upon instance deletion, all active, i.e. in a dialing state, within a script, or connected to an agent, calls are dropped

Preview campaigns
Upon instance deletion, only the calls not yet picked up by an agent are dropped. In-progress and connected calls are not affected

Otherwise, if there are still other records in the list, the method won't impact any calls.

The list of deleted records with completed calls, as well as their results, are archived and available for downloading in the Contact Center Administrator application (see here). Interaction results for dropped calls are not saved.

Note: This method does not delete contacts, activities, voice recordings, transcriptions, or screen recordings. This functionality is covered by other APIs.
